Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

message noun

also send a message, leave a message, give someone a message, phone message

classical

Cic. Fam. 4.12.1: nōn jūcundissimum mē nūntium vōbīs allātūrum
Traupman 261, 345: nūntius, message

nūntius, nūntiī m.

noun, second declension

a message, news

Also the messenger who brings it. A phone message is nūntius tēlephōnicus (M-O s.v. telephone message); Traupman gives the word among his computer terms too.

Examples

  • etsī sciō nōn jūcundissimum mē nūntium vōbīs allātūrum, tamen … vīsum est faciendum, quōquō modō rēs sē habēret, vōs certiōrēs facere.

    Although I know that the message I bring you is far from welcome, … I thought I should let you know how things stand, whatever they are.Cic. Fam. 4.12.1

  • Inest lepōs in nūntiō tuō magnus, mea Ampelisca.

    There’s great charm in your news, my Ampelisca.Plaut. Rud. 352

Other words

  • mandātum, mandātī n. — a message given to someone to deliver; instructions

    noun, second declension; usually plural, mandāta · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 7.14.1: L. Caesar mandāta Caesaris dētulit ad Pompejum; Caes. BG 1.35.1: lēgātōs cum hīs mandātīs mittit

    Lewis & Short: “a charge, order, commission”; mandāta dare, dēferre, to give, to deliver a message.

  • litterae, litterārum f. pl. — a letter, a written message

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 11.24.4: nē per litterās quidem aut per nūntium

See also information, forward, contact, communication.
